# UTF-8 C1 controls inside an escape, its intermediates or a CSI. xterm acts on
# the C1 and leaves the sequence, so what follows shows. herdr 0.9.1 ignores
# UTF-8 C1 controls (checked live for #15) and stays in the sequence. After ESC
# that can open a string that hides everything up to its end, and anywhere in a
# sequence it eats the next character as the sequence's final byte, one hidden
# letter at a time. Sightline shows what xterm shows and flags what herdr hides.
# Found by FuzzInjection (#70).
#
# herdr is also taken to ignore any other non-ASCII character inside an escape,
# as a parser that only decodes UTF-8 in plain text does. That part and the
# intermediate and CSI cases haven't been checked live. If herdr does otherwise,
# Sightline only flags more than it needs to.
# hidden: HIDDEN
# caught: Error: after
@ feed
A\e\u0085XHIDDEN after a NEL opens an SOS Error: x\e\\B
A\e\u0097XHIDDEN after an EPA opens an SOS Error: y\e\\B
A\e\u0085]0;HIDDEN after a NEL opens an OSC Error: z\aB
A\e\u0085PHIDDEN after a NEL opens a DCS Error: w\e\\B
A\e\u0085_HIDDEN on this line
HIDDEN on the next line Error: v\e\\B
\e\u0085H\e\u0085I\e\u0085D\e\u0085D\e\u0085E\e\u0085N eaten by ESC Error: u
\e(\u0085H\e(\u0085I\e(\u0085D\e(\u0085D\e(\u0085E\e(\u0085N eaten by an intermediate Error: t
\e[\u0085H\e[\u0085I\e[\u0085D\e[\u0085D\e[\u0085E\e[\u0085N eaten by a CSI Error: s
\e[1\u0085HIDDEN eaten by a CSI's parameters Error: r
A\eéXHIDDEN after an e acute opens an SOS Error: q\e\\B
A\e\xffXHIDDEN after invalid UTF-8 opens an SOS Error: p\e\\B
\e[éH\e[éI\e[éD\e[éD\e[éE\e[éN eaten by a CSI after an e acute Error: o
A\e]title\eéXHIDDEN after ESC and an e acute inside an OSC Error: n\e\\B
@ wait 2s
@ feed
Error: after
